classification.difficultyReason: Select the central observation, exclude it when finding the two half-medians, calculate IQR and transfer the five-number summary to a labelled boxplot. These are explicitly scaffolded routine linked procedures.

inlines.text: The pulse rates of 21 adult females are recorded.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the median, upper quartile, lower quartile and interquartile range.

answer.short: Median $=75$, upper quartile $=78.5$, lower quartile $=69.5$, interquartile range $=9$.
answer.worked:
There are 21 ordered values, so the median is the 11th value, $75$. Omit this value and divide the remaining values into two groups of 10.

The lower group's middle values are $69$ and $70$; the upper group's middle values are $78$ and $79$.

$$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{69+70}{2}\\Q_1&=69.5\\Q_3&=\frac{78+79}{2}\\Q_3&=78.5\\\text{IQR}&=78.5-69.5\\\text{IQR}&=9\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw a boxplot for this data.

answer.short: Boxplot with minimum $60$, lower quartile $69.5$, median $75$, upper quartile $78.5$ and maximum $90$.
answer.worked: Use a labelled pulse-rate scale. Draw the box from $69.5$ to $78.5$, with its median line at $75$. Extend the whiskers to the minimum $60$ and maximum $90$.

spec.description: Unfilled horizontal boxplot on a labelled pulse-rate scale; ordinary lines and labels use black.
